title: North America Sales Director, Energy Services at Caterpillar Sees GE Vernova as a Strong Incumbent in Utility Markets
expert: North America Sales Director, Energy Services at Caterpillar (competitor; ex-Schneider ~13 yrs, ex-Siemens)
verdict: A Caterpillar sales director who competes with GEV sees it as the default utility incumbent, but says shortages of large units (50 MW) are pushing some customers to 100 kW–500 kW units from unfamiliar or Asian suppliers.
thesis_impact: Tenet 2 (supply short): ↑ — 50 MW shortages and lengthening lead times push buyers to alternatives.
Tenet 5 (electrification): ↑ — incumbency wins utility work even at a higher price; GEV breadth less compartmentalized than Caterpillar.
Tenet 6 (order air pocket): ↑ — backlog carries revenue for the next year or two through order delays.
Tenet 1 (gas sold out): → — supports tightness, but share leaks at the small-unit end.
changes: Equipment lead times moving further out (expert, unquantified) vs SemiAnalysis 63–80 months (SB #65944): consistent.
Customers sourcing smaller units from new suppliers vs Jereh DC orders Rmb10.2B 3Q26 vs Rmb4.5B 2Q26 (SB #65781): consistent, share leak at the small end.
Backlog cushions an order pause (expert) vs 3Q26 backlog $197B and gas contracts 11GW vs ~20GW prior quarters (SB #62249, #62250): consistent with Tenet 6.
First read on utility switching behaviour; the 2026-11-06 expert call covered nuclear only.

Big-3 supply response: 🔴 **Shortages of 50 MW units push customers to 100 kW or 500 kW units from unfamiliar suppliers**, consistent with competitor Jereh DC orders Rmb10.2B in 3Q26 vs Rmb4.5B in 2Q26 (SB #65781): share-leak risk. → Tenet 2 (supply short) ↑
🟢 **Interconnection studies a couple of years, then three years to connect**; equipment lead times moving further out (unquantified), consistent with SemiAnalysis 63–80 month lead times (SB #65944).
GW contract adds cadence: 🟢 **Backlog sustains revenue for the next year or two** even if delays of half a year or a year pause orders (estimate), consistent with 3Q26 backlog $197B (SB #62249) despite gas contracts 11GW vs ~20GW in 1Q/2Q (SB #62250). → Tenet 6 (air pocket is sentiment) ↑
Electrification: 🟢 **Incumbent wins even when a challenger is cheaper** on switching risk for utilities with a billion-dollar budget; Trench deal (SB #62252) flagged as securing bushings and instrument transformers. → Tenet 5 (electrification) ↑
